package_info.why_malicious: These packages impersonate legitimate JavaScript libraries but contain obfuscated or plaintext code that, upon installation, exfiltrates sensitive files such as Kubernetes configuration and SSH keys to an external server (app.threatest.com) without user consent. The packages are deceptive in their metadata and behavior, indicating clear malicious intent.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During postinstall, the code reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config, collects system fingerprinting data (username, hostname, external IP), and exfiltrates this data via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code collects highly sensitive files and system information and sends them to an external server without user knowledge or consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A normal npm package should not access private SSH keys, Kubernetes configs, or exfiltrate data during installation. Legitimate postinstall scripts are typically used for build steps, not for data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A legitimate enterprise tool might collect diagnostic data with explicit user consent, but never private keys or configs.
key_indicators: Network exfiltration to hardcoded external domain (app.threatest.com)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During postinstall, the obfuscated code performs the same actions as the plaintext version: reads sensitive files and system info, then exfiltrates them to app.threatest.com.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscation is used to hide malicious intent, but the underlying behavior matches the plaintext version: unauthorized access and exfiltration of sensitive files.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Obfuscated postinstall scripts are highly unusual for open source packages, especially when accessing sensitive files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation may be used for commercial software protection, but not for open source npm packages, and never for exfiltrating secrets.
key_indicators: Same file access and exfiltration logic as plaintext version

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious npm package (e.g., @am-fe/hooks or @fixedwidthtable/fixedwidthtable).
Postinstall script executes, reading sensitive files (SSH keys, Kubernetes config) and collecting system fingerprinting data.
Script sends the collected data to the attacker's server (app.threatest.com) via HTTPS POST.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive credentials and system information.

behavioral_signatures: Collection of system fingerprinting data (username, hostname, external IP) during install
Network requests to hardcoded external domains during package installation
file_indicators: scripts/index.js with code accessing SSH or Kubernetes config
Presence of obfuscated or minified code in postinstall scripts
network_indicators: Outbound connections to 172.67.141.49 or 104.21.9.30 during npm install
Requests to api.ipify.org to obtain external IP
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts that access sensitive files such as ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config. Flag any package that sends data to external domains (especially app.threatest.com) or contains obfuscated code in install scripts. Use static analysis to detect file access patterns and hardcoded network destinations. Network monitoring can also reveal suspicious outbound connections during package installation.
